record.original_question: Are there plane billiards, other than ellipses, that posses s rational caustics with two different values of the rotation numbers? Same question for o uter billiards. Kaloshin and J. Zhang [129] studied the case of 1 /2 and 1 /3 caustics. They proved that, for a certain class of analytic deformations of a circle, the coexistence of such c austics implies that the deformation is trivial. Here is a weaker version of the previous problem. Let q0 ≥ 2 be an integer. A billiard table is called q0-rationally integrable is it possesses p/q-rational caustics for all 0 < p/q < 1/q0 (see [117]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A plane billiard is a strictly convex bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The billiard map $T$ acts on oriented chords (or, equivalently, on the cylinder of boundary point/inward direction pairs) by the law of reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection. A smooth convex curve $\Gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a caustic if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\Gamma$ remains tangent to $\Gamma$ after each reflection. To each caustic $\Gamma$ one associates a rotation number $\rho(\Gamma) \in (0,1/2]$ describing the average rotation per reflection of trajectories tangent to $\Gamma$. A caustic is called rational with rotation number $p/q$ (in lowest terms, $0<p/q<1/2$) if $\rho(\Gamma)=p/q$; equivalently, the trajectories tangent to $\Gamma$ are closed polygons of period $q$ winding $p$ times around $\Gamma$.

It is classical that every ellipse possesses rational caustics (confocal ellipses) for every admissible rotation number $p/q$.

An outer (dual) billiard about a strictly convex closed curve $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is the map of the exterior defined as follows: for a point $x$ outside $\gamma$, let $\ell$ be the tangent line from $x$ to $\gamma$ (oriented so that $\gamma$ lies to the right), touching $\gamma$ at $y$; then the image of $x$ is the reflection of $x$ through $y$. Caustics and rational caustics for outer billiards are defined analogously, as invariant curves carrying rotation number $p/q$.

Questions.
(a) Does there exist a plane (Birkhoff) billiard table, not bounded by an ellipse, that possesses rational caustics with at least two distinct rotation numbers $p_1/q_1 \ne p_2/q_2$?

(b) Same question for outer billiards: does there exist a strictly convex closed curve $\gamma$, not an ellipse, whose outer billiard map admits rational invariant caustics with at least two distinct rotation numbers?

(c) (Weaker version.) For an integer $q_0 \ge 2$, call a billiard table $q_0$-rationally integrable if it possesses a $p/q$-rational caustic for every rational $0 < p/q < 1/q_0$. Must every $q_0$-rationally integrable plane billiard be an ellipse?
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem remains open. Partial results exist: Kaloshin and J. Zhang showed that, for a class of analytic deformations of the circle, the coexistence of 1/2 and 1/3 rational caustics forces the deformation to be trivial; subsequent work (e.g. Koudjinan and others) extended non-coexistence results for 2- and 3-rational caustics near the circle, while studies of nearly circular billiards suggest possible families with coexisting 1/3 and 1/5 caustics at higher order. Kaloshin–Sorrentino proved a local rigidity theorem for integrable deformations of an ellipse. No example of a non-elliptic billiard with two rational caustics is known, and the full conjecture (including for outer billiards and the $q_0$-rationally integrable variant) is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On non-coexistence of 2- & 3-rational caustics in nearly circular billiard tables (Koudjinan)
status_evidence.snippet: On non-coexistence of 2- & 3-rational caustics in nearly circular billiard tables.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: non-coexistence of 1/2 and 1/3 rational caustics for nearly circular tables.

status_evidence.title: Density of convex billiards with rational caustics (Kaloshin–Zhang)
status_evidence.snippet: The set of billiard boundaries with rational caustics is dense among convex domains.
status_evidence.claim: Kaloshin–Zhang work on rational caustics, including the coexistence question near the circle.

status_evidence.title: On the integrability of Birkhoff billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing Birkhoff conjecture and rigidity of integrable billiards near the ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Local rigidity results around ellipses but the global question for two rational caustics remains open.

status_evidence.title: High-order persistence of resonant caustics in perturbed circular billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Persistence of resonant caustics under perturbations of the circle.
status_evidence.claim: Investigations on coexistence of resonant caustics (e.g. periods 3 and 5) of perturbed circles.
